proposal.blind_spot: The current metrics show memory-boundness but cannot tell whether a kernel is truly DRAM-bandwidth-saturated (only fewer bytes helps) or latency/occupancy-limited with bandwidth headroom (more resident warps or loads-in-flight would speed it up).

rationale.sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustain: HIGH -> occupancy is fine; stop tuning launch config, cut DRAM bytes (fuse ops, drop intermediates, narrower dtype) or accept roofline / LOW -> raise occupancy via smaller tiles, fewer registers per thread, better block size, larger grid to convert DRAM headroom into speedup
rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH with DRAM ~90%+ -> warps wait on saturated bandwidth, ILP/launch changes are futile, reduce bytes moved / LOW (or HIGH with DRAM only ~70-80%) -> add memory-level parallelism (more warps, ILP, prefetch) or, if stalls are elsewhere, restructure the algorithm (warp-level reductions, fewer barriers)
